title: The UK charity shop
paragraphs: What do you do with old stuff? That top you bought for a party three years ago, for example. You wore it once and it's been hanging in your wardrobe ever since. You could throw it away, but that seems wasteful – after all it's still perfectly usable. So, what to do? In the UK, we might take it to a charity shop.

The first charity shops appeared in Britain in the 19th Century. The Salvation Army, a UK charity, was one of the first to run a second-hand clothing shop to provide the impoverished and needy with affordable clothes. This was followed by charities such as the British Red Cross, who also relieved hardship and raised money for the war effort during World War Two. The modern form we know today was opened in 1947 by Oxfam. These days, charity shops are a common sight with around 11,200 shops across the UK, according to the Charity Retail Association. During business hours any member of the public can donate their unwanted items to a charity shop – clothes, books, electronics, furniture. Most charity shops will take anything. These items are checked for wear and tear and if found still serviceable, priced up to be sold at a heavily discounted price.

For many, this is a win-win situation. To the charity, it means a valuable source of revenue, which they can use to pursue their charitable aim. To the consumer, it provides the opportunity to buy, often extremely cheaply, items and clothes. Though previously owned, they are durable. To the donator, it declutters and may help to assuage consumer guilt. “You can make a pretty good case to yourself that you are doing good, because what you are doing is going towards a charitable cause [and] you are saving stuff from landfill,” Clare Press, fashion journalist and sustainable style advocate, tells the Guardian. Indeed, approximately £140 million worth of clothing alone goes into landfill each year, according to UK charity WRAP, the Waste and Resources Action Programme.

There are sometimes hidden treasures for the buyers, too. On more than one occasion a buyer has purchased something very cheaply, only to later discover its true value – such as a screen print bought for 99p and later found to be by English artist Ben Nicholson. It sold at auction for £4,200. So next time you need to rid yourself of something, spare a thought for the charity shop – after all, charity begins at home!

vocabulary.example: She hung her dresses in the wooden wardrobe by the window.
vocabulary.translation: 她把连衣裙挂在窗边的木质衣柜里。

vocabulary.term: charity shop [ˈtʃærəti ʃɒp] n. 慈善商店
vocabulary.entry: charity shop [ˈtʃærəti ʃɒp] n. 慈善商店
vocabulary.example: I found a vintage jacket in excellent condition at the local charity shop.
vocabulary.translation: 我在当地的慈善商店淘到一件保存完好的复古夹克。

vocabulary.term: Salvation Army [ˈsælveɪʃn ˈɑːmi] 救世军（慈善组织）
vocabulary.entry: Salvation Army [ˈsælveɪʃn ˈɑːmi] 救世军（慈善组织）
vocabulary.example: The Salvation Army distributes hot meals to the homeless every winter.
vocabulary.translation: 救世军每年冬天都会为无家可归者分发热餐。

vocabulary.example: The program provides educational support for children in impoverished rural areas.
vocabulary.translation: 该项目为贫困农村地区的儿童提供教育支持。

vocabulary.term: relieve hardship [rɪˈliːv ˈhɑːdʃɪp] 缓解困难
vocabulary.entry: relieve hardship [rɪˈliːv ˈhɑːdʃɪp] 缓解困难
vocabulary.example: The government launched a scheme to relieve financial hardship for low-income families.
vocabulary.translation: 政府推出了一项计划，以缓解低收入家庭的经济困难。

vocabulary.term: wear and tear [weə ənd teə] 磨损；损耗
vocabulary.entry: wear and tear [weə ənd teə] 磨损；损耗
vocabulary.example: The insurance policy covers damage caused by normal wear and tear.
vocabulary.translation: 这份保险涵盖正常磨损造成的损坏。

vocabulary.term: serviceable [ˈsɜːvɪsəbl] adj. 可用的；耐用的
vocabulary.entry: serviceable [ˈsɜːvɪsəbl] adj. 可用的；耐用的
vocabulary.example: These tools are old but still serviceable for basic repairs.
vocabulary.translation: 这些工具虽然旧，但用于基本维修仍然可用。

vocabulary.example: Members of the club can purchase tickets at a discounted price.
vocabulary.translation: 俱乐部会员可以以折扣价购买门票。

vocabulary.example: The majority of the charity's revenue comes from donations and fundraisers.
vocabulary.translation: 该慈善机构的大部分收入来自捐赠和筹款活动。

vocabulary.example: This brand is known for producing durable outdoor clothing.
vocabulary.translation: 该品牌以生产耐用的户外服装而闻名。

vocabulary.example: We need to declutter the attic before we can use it as a storage space.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要先清理阁楼的杂物，才能把它用作储物间。

vocabulary.example: A hot drink can assuage the discomfort of a cold.
vocabulary.translation: 一杯热饮可以缓解感冒带来的不适感。

vocabulary.example: Reducing food waste helps minimize the amount of trash sent to landfill.
vocabulary.translation: 减少食物浪费有助于减少送往垃圾填埋场的垃圾量。

vocabulary.term: screen print [skriːn prɪnt] 丝网印刷品
vocabulary.entry: screen print [skriːn prɪnt] 丝网印刷品
vocabulary.example: The artist sold limited-edition screen prints of her latest work.
vocabulary.translation: 这位艺术家出售了她最新作品的限量版丝网印刷品。

vocabulary.example: Rare books and manuscripts will be sold at auction next month.
vocabulary.translation: 珍本书籍和手稿将于下个月进行拍卖。

vocabulary.term: rid oneself of sth [rɪd wʌnˈself ɒv sth] 处理掉某物
vocabulary.entry: rid oneself of sth [rɪd wʌnˈself ɒv sth] 处理掉某物
vocabulary.example: He finally rid himself of the old furniture he'd been storing for years.
vocabulary.translation: 他终于把存放了多年的旧家具处理掉了。

vocabulary.term: spare a thought for [speə ə θɔːt fɔː] 考虑到；想到
vocabulary.entry: spare a thought for [speə ə θɔːt fɔː] 考虑到；想到
vocabulary.example: As we celebrate the holiday, spare a thought for those working in essential services.
vocabulary.translation: 在我们庆祝节日的同时，想想那些在必要服务岗位上工作的人。

vocabulary.term: charity begins at home [ˈtʃærəti bɪˈɡɪnz æt həʊm] 慈善始于自家（谚语）
vocabulary.entry: charity begins at home [ˈtʃærəti bɪˈɡɪnz æt həʊm] 慈善始于自家（谚语）
vocabulary.example: She always helps her family first—after all, charity begins at home.
vocabulary.translation: 她总是先帮助家人——毕竟，慈善始于自家。

vocabulary.example: Buying second-hand furniture is a cost-effective way to furnish an apartment.
vocabulary.translation: 购买二手家具是布置公寓的经济实惠之选。

vocabulary.example: She decided to pursue a career in environmental conservation.
vocabulary.translation: 她决定从事环境保护方面的工作。

sentences.english: What do you do with old stuff?
That top you bought for a party three years ago, for example. You wore it once and it's been hanging in your wardrobe ever since.
sentences.chinese: 比如三年前为派对买的那件上衣，你只穿过一次，之后就一直挂在衣柜里。

sentences.english: You could throw it away, but that seems wasteful – after all it's still perfectly usable.
sentences.chinese: 你可以扔掉它，但这似乎很浪费——毕竟它完全能穿。

sentences.english: In the UK, we might take it to a charity shop.
sentences.chinese: 在英国，人们可能会把它送到慈善商店。

sentences.english: The first charity shops appeared in Britain in the 19th Century.
sentences.chinese: 英国最早的慈善商店出现在19世纪。

sentences.english: The Salvation Army, a UK charity, was one of the first to run a second-hand clothing shop to provide the impoverished and needy with affordable clothes.
sentences.chinese: 英国慈善机构“救世军”是最早经营二手服装店的机构之一，旨在为贫困和有需要的人提供价格实惠的衣物。

sentences.english: This was followed by charities such as the British Red Cross, who also relieved hardship and raised money for the war effort during World War Two.
sentences.chinese: 随后，英国红十字会等慈善机构也加入其中，它们在二战期间还通过这种方式摆脱贫困带来困难并为战争筹集资金。

sentences.english: The modern form we know today was opened in 1947 by Oxfam.
sentences.chinese: 我们如今熟知的现代慈善商店形式由乐施会于1947年开创。

sentences.english: These days, charity shops are a common sight with around 11,200 shops across the UK, according to the Charity Retail Association.
sentences.chinese: 据慈善零售协会数据，如今慈善商店在英国随处可见，全国约有11200家。

sentences.english: During business hours any member of the public can donate their unwanted items to a charity shop – clothes, books, electronics, furniture. Most charity shops will take anything.
sentences.chinese: 在营业时间内，任何公众都可以将不需要的物品捐赠给慈善商店——衣物、书籍、电子产品、家具等，大多数慈善商店几乎接受任何物品。

sentences.english: These items are checked for wear and tear and if found still serviceable, priced up to be sold at a heavily discounted price.
sentences.chinese: 这些物品会被检查是否有磨损，若仍可使用，就会定价并以大幅折扣出售。

sentences.english: For many, this is a win-win situation.
sentences.chinese: 对许多人来说，这是双赢。

sentences.english: To the charity, it means a valuable source of revenue, which they can use to pursue their charitable aim. To the consumer, it provides the opportunity to buy, often extremely cheaply, items and clothes. Though previously owned, they are durable. To the donator, it declutters and may help to assuage consumer guilt.
sentences.chinese: 对慈善机构而言，这是宝贵的收入来源，可用于实现其慈善目标；对消费者而言，这提供了以极低价格购买物品和衣物的机会，这些物品虽为二手，但依然耐用；对捐赠者而言，这能清理杂物，并有助于减轻消费内疚感。

sentences.english: “You can make a pretty good case to yourself that you are doing good, because what you are doing is going towards a charitable cause [and] you are saving stuff from landfill,” Clare Press, fashion journalist and sustainable style advocate, tells the Guardian.
sentences.chinese: 时尚记者兼可持续时尚倡导者克莱尔・普雷斯在接受《卫报》采访时表示：“你可以说服自己正在做善事，因为你所做的事既支持了慈善事业，又避免了物品被扔进landfill（垃圾填埋场）。”

sentences.english: Indeed, approximately £140 million worth of clothing alone goes into landfill each year, according to UK charity WRAP, the Waste and Resources Action Programme.
sentences.chinese: 事实上，据英国慈善机构“废弃物与资源行动计划”（WRAP）统计，仅衣物一项，每年就有约1.4亿英镑的衣物被扔进垃圾填埋场。

sentences.english: There are sometimes hidden treasures for the buyers, too.
sentences.chinese: 对买家而言，有时还能发现隐藏的宝藏。

sentences.english: On more than one occasion a buyer has purchased something very cheaply, only to later discover its true value – such as a screen print bought for 99p and later found to be by English artist Ben Nicholson. It sold at auction for £4,200.
sentences.chinese: 不止一次，有人以极低价格购得物品，后来却发现其真正价值——例如一幅以99便士购得的丝网印刷品，后来被认定为英国艺术家本・尼科尔森的作品，最终在拍卖会上以4200英镑售出。

sentences.english: So next time you need to rid yourself of something, spare a thought for the charity shop – after all, charity begins at home!
sentences.chinese: 因此，下次你想处理物品时，不妨想想慈善商店——毕竟，慈善始于自家！
